description: Number decoding edge cases – trailing zeros, exponent forms, negative zero

tests.name: parses number with trailing zeros in fractional part
parses negative number with positive exponent
parses uppercase exponent with negative sign
parses negative zero as zero
tests.note: Negative zero decodes to 0; most host environments do not distinguish -0 from 0

tests.name: parses negative zero with fractional part
parses array with mixed numeric forms
tests.note: Decoders normalize all numeric forms to host numeric values

tests.name: treats leading zero as string not number
parses zero with exponent as number
treats unquoted leading-zero number as string
treats leading-zeros in array as strings
treats unquoted negative leading-zero number as string
treats bare fraction without integer part as string
tests.note: Outside the number grammar, so a host parser would read 0.5 and corrupt the round-trip

tests.name: treats integer with trailing dot as string
treats leading-plus integer as string
tests.note: The grammar admits only an optional leading minus, so +1 stays a string

tests.name: treats leading-plus tokens in array as strings
tests.note: The grammar admits only an optional leading minus, so leading-plus cells stay strings

tests.name: treats Infinity and NaN tokens as strings
treats hex and underscore-separated tokens as strings
tests.note: Host parsers that accept these forms have a wider grammar than the spec permits
